Wáng Zǎi, Military Commissioner of Bīn-Níng, was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhōng-Wǔ.
Mào-Yuán was
the son of Qī-Yào;
Zǎi was
the son of Zhì-Xīng.
Wáng Qī-Yào is mentioned in volume 230, Dè-Zōng, Xīng-Yuán 1st year.
Wáng Zhì-Xīng first appeared in volume 227, Jiàn-Zhōng 2nd year.
Dù Mù, the Cìshǐ of Huángzhōu, submitted a letter to Lǐ Déyù,
stating:
"I once asked Dǒng Zhòngzhì, a general from Huáixī, why the forces from the three prefectures failed to defeat [Càizhōu] for four years.
Zhòngzhì believed the reason was that the imperial court's conscripted troops were too mixed,
and the guest armies were few in number.
As they could not form an army on their own,
they had to be attached to local commanders.
Being weak and lacking strength,
and with disunity of purpose,
they often suffered defeats.
Therefore, in the first two years of fighting,
when they fought, they were always victorious,
but this meant many guest troops were killed.
After two years,
with the guest troops exhausted and few,
they only fought against the full armies of Chén-Xǔ and Héyáng.
Chén-Xǔ
refers to Lǐ Guāngyán's troops;
Héyáng
refers to Wū Zhòngyìn's troops.
Tángzhōu refers to Lǐ Sù's troops.
At that time, if the imperial court had ordered Èzhōu, Shòuzhōu, and Tángzhōu merely to guard their borders,
without advancing to battle,
and only used the full armies of Chén-Xǔ and Zhèng-Huá,
attaching archers from Xuān-Rùn
to guard the passes,
then within a year,
Càizhōu would have been no more.
Now, the rebellion in Shàngdǎng
is different from Huáixī.
Huáixī had been a bandit stronghold for only fifty years;
its people savored the richness of banditry,
saw its advantages,
their customs became deeply entrenched,
and their power was already established.
They considered themselves unmatched by any army in the realm,
with deep roots and a wide source,
making their subjugation indeed difficult.
Shàngdǎng, however, is not like that.
Since Ān and Shǐ moved south,
it has not been greatly subordinated;
during Sùzōng's time, Cài Xīdé attacked Shàngdǎng but could not conquer it.
They always displayed loyalty and righteousness;
thus, Ní Gōng Bàozhēn was able to put Tián Yuè in distress
and rout Zhū Tāo,
often using his isolated, poor, and suffering army
to decisively defeat the strong and overbearing forces of Hèshuò.
This evidence shows
that the people's hearts are loyal and pure,
their customs dedicated and unified,
which can be fully observed.
When Liú Wù died,
Cóngjiàn sought to succeed him,
and those who supported him
were only the two thousand central army troops who came with him from Yùnzhōu.
'Fú Tóng'
is like the current vernacular 'fúhé'.
Liú Wù moved from being the commander of Yùn to Huá,
and from Huá to Lù;
the two thousand Yùn soldiers indeed followed him.
In the late Táng, they were called 'yuáncóng'.
He was then given command.
Now, it has only been just over twenty years—
according to Bǎolì first year,
when Liú Cóngjiàn was granted the title of Zhāoyì Jiédù,
it was only nineteen years until this year.
The old veterans still survive;
even if one wanted to coerce them,
they would certainly not obey.
Now, although Chéngdé and Wèibó are fully committed to displaying loyalty and obedience,
they will do no more than besiege a city,
attack a stronghold,
and capture children and the elderly.
If ten thousand men from Héyáng were to form a rampart,
blocking the mouth of Tiānjǐng,
Tiānjǐng Guān is south of Jìnchéng Xiàn in Zézhōu,
also known as Tàiháng Guān.
South of the pass are three Tiānjǐng springs,
hence the name.
Dù Mù's statement here
intends to prevent the people of Lù from gazing south towards Huái and Luò.
Do not engage them in battle.
Just use the two armies of Zhōngwǔ and Wǔníng—
Zhōngwǔ
refers to the Chén-Xǔ troops;
Wǔníng
refers to the Xúzhōu troops—
and two thousand archers from Xuān-Rùn,
to strike directly at Shàngdǎng.
Within a few months,
their nest will surely be overturned!"
At that time, Déyù was in charge of the Zé-Lù pacification,
and largely adopted Mù's advice.
The Emperor, though outwardly honoring Chóu Shìliáng,
secretly detested him.
Shìliáng somewhat sensed this,
and thus requested a sinecure due to old age and illness.
An imperial edict appointed him Left Guard Supreme General, concurrently Supervisor of the Inner Palace Secretariat, and Manager of Palace Affairs.
Manager of Inner Palace Secretariat Affairs.
Lǐ Déyù said to the Emperor:
"Commentators all say that Liú Wù had merits—
Liú Wù's merit was the execution of Lǐ Shīdào—
and that full grace and courtesy should be extended.
I request that the hundred officials deliberate on this,
to satisfy public sentiment."
The Emperor said:
"What merit did Wù have?
At that time, he was compelled to save himself,
it was not from a long-standing desire to serve the country.
Even if he had merits,
with father and son serving as generals and prime ministers for over twenty years,
the state has sufficiently rewarded him.
How can Zhěn still establish himself?
I believe that those with merits should be conspicuously rewarded,
but those with crimes should also not be casually exempted."
Déyù said:
"Your Majesty's words
indeed grasp the essence of governing the state."
In the fifth month,
Lǐ Déyù stated that the Crown Prince's Mentor and part-time official, Lǐ Zōngmǐn, was colluding with Liú Cóngjiàn,
and should not be stationed in Dōngdū.
On the day of Wùxū,
Zōngmǐn was appointed Cìshǐ of Húzhōu.
Historians say Lǐ Déyù bore a grudge.
The 'Kǎoyì' states: The 'Xiàntì Jì' records:
"On the nineteenth day of the fourth month,
the Emperor said: 'Lǐ Zōngmǐn in Dōngdū,
I heard that recently he has been colluding with Cóngjiàn.
How should the Zé-Lù matter be handled?
He should be given another official post,
not allowed to stay in Dōngdū.'
Déyù said: 'Your subjects will discuss it further.'
The Emperor then said: 'He cannot be given a frontier command;
only a distant prefecture!'
Déyù then reported: 'He must be given a prefecture!'"
This was likely Déyù, due to his old resentment, using the Liú Zhěn affair to harm Zōngmǐn,
and fearing criticism, thus recording this passage in the 'Xiàntì Jì' to conceal his tracks.
We now follow the 'Shílù'.
Wáng Màoyuán, the Jiédùshǐ of Héyáng, with three thousand infantry and cavalry, guarded Wànshàn;
The 'Jiǔyù Zhì' states: Huáizhōu Hénèi Xiàn has Wànshàn Zhèn.
Mángchē Guān is Āngchē Guān.
Wèi Shōu's 'Dìxíng Zhì' states: Shàngdǎng Jùn Zhān Xiàn has Āngchē Líng.
Its location should be west of Shíhuì Guān, in the southeast border of Táng Yízhōu.
The 'Xīn Táng Zhì' states: Lùzhōu Wǔxiāng Xiàn has Āngchē Guān to its north.
The 'Jiǔyù Zhì' states: Liáozhōu Liáoshān Xiàn has Yúshè Zhèn,
which was Táng's Yúshè Xiàn.
Sòng Bái said: Yúshè Xiàn was established in Suí Kāihuáng sixteenth year,
and is now the seat of Lùzhōu Xiāngyuán Xiàn.
It is named after the old city of Yúshè northwest of the present county.
They plundered Yáoshān;
Yáoshān was originally Bǎirén Xiàn,
renamed in Tiānbǎo first year,
and belonged to Xíngzhōu.
Sòng Bái said: Named after the land of the great recluse Yáo.
Míng,
pronounced míng.
Five hundred infantry reinforced
Jìshì.
Jìshì was originally the land of Hàn Yīshì Xiàn.
Later Wèi established Jìshì Jùn and Jìshì Xiàn south of the old Yīshì Xiàn city.
Suí abolished the Jùn and kept the Xiàn,
Táng belonged to Jìnzhōu.
The 'Jiǔyù Zhì' states: 280 lǐ northeast of the prefecture.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
an edict stripped Liú Cóngjiàn and his son Zhěn of their official titles and ranks.
Yuán Kuí was appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Northern Front of Zé-Lù,
Hé Hóngjìng as Pacification Commissioner for the Southern Front,
to jointly attack with Yí Xíng, Liú Miǎn, and Màoyuán.
Formerly, when there were those who established themselves independently in the various prefectures of Héshuò,
the imperial court would first send a mourning and sacrificial envoy,
then an envoy for bestowal of titles and posthumous honors.
A pacification and consolation envoy would follow to assess the military situation.
If it was absolutely impossible to grant them a *jié* (credentials of a military governor),
then a different official post would be created;
only after the army refused to let them leave,
would military force then be employed.
Thus, it often took half a year,
during which the army was able to repair and prepare itself.
At this point,
the prime minister also wished to first send an envoy to persuade them,
but the Emperor immediately ordered the issuance of an edict to suppress them.
The *Kǎoyì* says: The *Xiàntì Jì* says:
"On the eleventh day of the fifth month,
Lǐ Déyù was ill,
having already requested leave and being at home.
Prime Minister Lǐ Shēn also requested leave on that day.
Prime Minister Lǐ Ràngyí was in audience alone,
and the Emperor then decided on the intention to attack and suppress.
After Prime Minister Lǐ returned to the *Zhōngshū* (Central Secretariat),
he recorded the imperial will on four sheets of paper,
ordering Déyù to draft the edict.
It was sealed and submitted late in the evening,
and the imperial decree for the disposition was issued the next day."
The old *Běnjì* (Annals) states that
an edict to suppress Liú Zhěn was issued in the ninth month.
Now we follow the *Shílù* (Veritable Records).
The army marched out and encamped at Zhàozhōu.
The *Jiǔyù Zhì* says: From Zhènzhōu south to Zhàozhōu is ninety-five *lǐ*.
On the 18th *rén yín* (day),
Cuī Xuán, a Hanlin Academician and Grand Academician-in-waiting, was appointed *Zhōngshū Shìláng* (Vice Director of the Central Secretariat) and *Tóng Píngzhāngshì* (concurrently a chancellor).
The first hall of the Hanlin Academicians was the *Chéngzhǐ Tīng* (Hall of the Grand Academician-in-waiting),
and it was held by the Hanlin Academician with the longest service.
The *Kǎoyì* says: The *Shílù* states that
Lǐ Ràngyí recommended Xuán for prime minister.
Now we follow the *Bǔ Guóshǐ* (Supplement to the National History).
He was the son of Cuī Yuánlüè.
Cuī Yuánlüè is mentioned in volume 223, Jìngzōng, Bǎolì first year.
He was appointed by Xuán's name,
and ordered to draft the edict,
which neither the prime minister nor the privy council knew about.
At that time, the Privy Councilors Liú Xíngshēn and Yáng Qīnyì were both earnest and sincere,
and dared not meddle in affairs,
but the old eunuchs criticized them saying:
"This is because Liú and Yáng are timid and cowardly,
and have thus corrupted the old customs."
Cóng was
the son of Gāndù.
Wéi Gāndù was *Lìbù Lángzhōng* (Director of the Bureau of Personnel) during Emperor Xiànzōng's reign.

On the 19th, Lǐ Yànzuǒ, *Wǔníng Jiédùshǐ* (Military Governor of Wǔníng), was appointed *Jìnjiàng Xíngyíng Zhūjūn Jiédù Zhāotǎoshǐ* (Military Governor and Commander-in-Chief of the various armies of Jìn and Jiàng mobile camps).
On the 20th, Liú Miǎn returned to Tàiyuán from Dàizhōu.
This was because the Huíhú had already been defeated and fled.
On the 21st, the Wàngxiān Guàn (Observatory of Immortals) was built within the Forbidden City.
The *Huìyào* says:
In this year, the Wàngxiān Lóu (Observatory of Immortals Tower) and its corridors and rooms, totaling five hundred and thirty-nine sections, were repaired.
*Guàn* (觀),
pronounced as *gǔ wán fān*.
In the sixth month,
Wáng Màoyuán dispatched his *Bīngmǎshǐ* (Commander of Horse and Foot Soldiers) Mǎ Jì and others to lead two thousand infantry and cavalry to camp at Kēdòudiàn south of Tiānjǐng Guān.
Liú Zhěn dispatched his *Yánèi Shíjiàng* (Ten-General of the Inner Palace) Xuē Màoqīng to lead two thousand of his personal troops to resist them.
On the 23rd, the Qíjiásī Khan dispatched General Wēn Wǔhé to present tribute.
The Emperor bestowed a letter upon him,
admonishing him to quickly pacify the Huíhú and Hēichēzǐ,
and then sent an envoy to confer the imperial mandate.
On the 24th *guǐ yǒu* (day),
Qiú Shìliáng retired from office as *Zuǒwèi Shàngjiàngjūn* (General-in-Chief of the Left Guard) and *Nèishì Jiān* (Director of the Palace Domestic Service).
His partisans escorted him back to his private residence,
where Shìliáng taught them the art of consolidating power and favor, saying:
"The Son of Heaven must not be allowed to be idle.
He should always be entertained with extravagance and luxury,
so that he daily enjoys new and grand things,
leaving no time for other matters.
Only then can we achieve our ambitions.
Be careful not to let him read books
or associate with Confucian scholars.
If he learns about the rise and fall of previous dynasties,
he will become worried and fearful in his heart,
and then we will be alienated and dismissed."
His partisans bowed in thanks and departed.
Observing Qiú Shìliáng's teachings to his partisans,
how could eunuchs ever be considered close associates!
On the 25th *bǐng zǐ* (day),
an edict was issued to Wáng Yuánkuí, Lǐ Yànzuǒ, Liú Miǎn, Wáng Màoyuán, and Hé Hóngjìng to advance simultaneously along five routes in mid-July.
Any request for surrender from Liú Zhěn was not to be accepted.
Another edict ordered Liú Miǎn to personally lead troops to take the Yǎngchē Guān route to approach the enemy territory.
Yǎngchē Guān is also known as Ángchē Guān.
On the 26th, Shàng Bìbì, *Jiédùshǐ* of Tǔbō Shànzhōu,
came from a family that had served as prime ministers to Tǔbō for generations.
Bìbì loved to read books
and did not enjoy officialdom.
His countrymen respected him.
When he was over forty years old,
Yítài Zànpǔ forced him to take up office,
making him governor of Shànzhōu.
Yítài was
the brother of Dámó,
and died in the third year of Kāichéng of Wénzōng.
*Qiáng* (強),
pronounced as *qí liǎng fān*.
He possessed stratagem and foresight,
and trained his soldiers to be numerous and exceptionally brave.
Although Lùn Kǒngrè claimed to be a righteous army,
he actually plotted to usurp the throne.
The uprising of Lùn Kǒngrè began in the second year of the previous volume.
Fearing that he would be attacked from behind,
he wished to first destroy him.
In this month,
he launched a large army to attack Bìbì,
with flags, banners, and various animals stretching for a thousand *lǐ* without interruption.
When they reached Zhènxī,
the Zhènxī army was
one hundred and eighty *lǐ* west of Hézhōu.
pronounced as *xǔ jiù fān*.
Heavenly fire burned and killed over ten auxiliary generals,
and hundreds of animals.
Kǒngrè was dismayed by this,
and hesitated, not advancing.
Bìbì said to his subordinates:
"Kǒngrè's arrival
views me as an ant,
thinking I am not worth slaughtering.
Now that he has encountered a heavenly disaster,
he hesitates and does not advance.
I had better go forth and submit to him to make him retreat,
making his ambition even more arrogant and causing him to lower his guard,
then we can make our plans."
So, he sent an envoy with gold, silk, cattle, and wine to reward the army,
and also sent a letter saying:
"Your Excellency has raised a righteous army to assist the nation in its difficulties;
within the entire territory,
who does not follow your example!
If you were to send even one messenger,
and bestow a brief note,
how dare I not obey your command!
Why must you trouble your soldiers and people so far,
and personally come to this humble fief!
Bìbì's nature is foolish and reclusive,
I only enjoy reading books.
The former Zànpǔ appointed me to this border region,
which is truly an inappropriate position.
Day and night I am ashamed and fearful,
only seeking to retire to my fields and home.
If Your Excellency would grant me retirement,
and allow me to return to my homeland,
it would fulfill my lifelong wish."
*Qiè* (愜),
pronounced as *qì yè fān*.
Kǒngrè showed the letter to all his generals, saying:
"Bìbì only holds books,
how could he know how to use an army!
When I obtain the country,
I shall appoint him as prime minister,
and let him stay at home,
he is useless otherwise."
Then he wrote another letter,
replying graciously,
and led his troops back.
When Bìbì heard of this,
he slapped his thigh and laughed, saying:
"If our country has no ruler,
then we will return to the Great Táng,
how can we serve these dogs and rats!"
In the autumn,
seventh month,
Lú Jūn, *Shānnán Dōngdào Jiédùshǐ* (Military Governor of Shānnán East Circuit), was appointed *Zhāoyì Jiédù Zhāofǔshǐ* (Military Governor and Pacification Commissioner of Zhāoyì).
The imperial court considered Jūn to be generous and benevolent in Xiāngyáng,
having gained the hearts of the people,
and therefore sent him to govern Zhāoyì to conciliate them.

On the 28th, the Emperor dispatched Lǐ Huí, *Xíngbù Shìláng* (Vice Minister of Punishments) and concurrent *Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng* (Imperial Censor-in-Chief), to pacify the three prefectures north of the Yellow River,
ordering Yōuzhōu to quickly pacify the Huíhú while the autumn was early,
and Zhèn and Wèi to quickly pacify Zélù.
Huí was
the eighth-generation descendant of Tàizǔ.
Tàizǔ's sixth son Yī begot Délíang,
six generations to Huí.
On the *jiǎ chén* (day),
Lǐ Déyù addressed the Emperor, saying:
"Your servant observes that in previous military campaigns in Héshuò,
the various circuits profited from moving beyond their borders to rely on the *Dùzhī* (Ministry of Finance).
Some secretly communicated with the rebels,
borrowing a county or a stockade to occupy it,
claiming it as their achievement,
and idly consuming transported provisions,
thus prolonging the campaign for years.
Now I request that an imperial decree be issued to all armies,
ordering Wáng Yuánkuí to take Xíngzhōu,
Hé Hóngjìng to take Míngzhōu,
Wáng Màoyuán to take Zézhōu,
and Lǐ Yànzuǒ and Liú Miǎn to take Lùzhōu,
but they must not take any counties (beyond these primary objectives)."
The Emperor assented to this.
Lǐ Yànzuǒ, Jìn-Jiàng Xíngyíng Jiédùshǐ, after departing from Xúzhōu,
marched very slowly.
He also requested a troop休兵 at Jiàngzhōu
and additional soldiers.
Lǐ Déyù spoke to the emperor, saying:
“Yànzuǒ is loitering and looking around,
showing no intention of pursuing the rebels.
All his requests should not be granted.
An imperial edict should be issued to sternly reprimand him,
ordering him to advance his army to Yìchéng.”
The Jiǔyù Zhì states: Yìchéng Xiàn is one hundred lǐ northeast of Jiàngzhōu.
Sòng Bái said: Yìchéng was originally the territory of Hàn's Jiàng Xiàn.
Later, Wèi Míngdì established Běijiàng Xiàn east of Qǔwò Xiàn.
The Suí dynasty changed its name to Yìchéng Xiàn,
named after the ancient city of Yìchéng east of the county.
Déyù then requested that Shí Xióng, Tiāndé Fángyùshǐ, be made Yànzuǒ's deputy,
and upon his arrival at the army,
he should replace Yànzuǒ.
On the Yǐsì day,
Xióng was appointed Jìn-Jiàng Xíngyíng Jiédù Fùshǐ,
and Yànzuǒ was ordered by edict to advance and garrison at Yìchéng.
Liú Zhěn submitted a memorial to state his case:
“My late father, Cóngjiàn, exonerated Lǐ Xùn
and spoke of the crimes of Chóu Shìliáng.
The matter is seen in Volume 245, Wénzōng, Kāichéng first year.
為 (wèi),
read as yú.
It is said that my father secretly harbored deviant ambitions,
which is why I dared not bring my entire clan to submit to the court.
I beg Your Majesty to show a little leniency and understanding,
and spare my entire region!”
Hé Hóngjìng also presented a memorial to exonerate him,
but both were not granted.
When Lǐ Huí arrived at Héshuò,
Hé Hóngjìng, Wáng Yuánkuí, and Zhāng Zhòngwǔ all put on their quivers and bows and went out to the suburbs to welcome him,
standing on the left side of the road,
not daring to let their attendants hold their horses,
allowing the emissary to go first.
制使 (zhìshǐ)
was used to distinguish from the eunuchs’ imperial envoys.
This had not happened before.
Since the outbreak of war,
referring to after the Tiānbǎo era.
the three garrisons had never failed to obey an imperial edict.
Wáng Yuánkuí reported that he had captured Xuānwù Zhà,
Xuānwù Zhà should be northeast of Yáoshān Xiàn.
Liú Zhěn sent troops to rescue Yáoshān,
but Yuánkuí defeated them.
An imperial edict sternly reprimanded Lǐ Yànzuǒ, Liú Miǎn, and Wáng Màoyuán,
ordering them to quickly advance their troops to press the rebel territory,
and also cited Yuánkuí’s achievements to motivate them.
Yuánkuí was given the additional title of Tóng Píngzhāngshì.
In the eighth month,
on the Yǐchǒu day,
Lǐ Pī, a major general of Zhāoyì, surrendered.
Some deliberators suggested that the rebels deliberately sent Pī to surrender,
hoping to mislead the government army.
Lǐ Déyù spoke to the emperor, saying:
“It has been half a year since the war began,
and there have been no surrenders.
Now, why question whether it is sincere or deceitful?
We must generously reward him to encourage future surrenders,
but just don't place him in a critical position.”
29The emperor leisurely remarked:
“Wénzōng liked to listen to outside opinions,
and the remonstrance officials often spoke on matters without signing their names,
like anonymous letters.”
Lǐ Déyù said:
“When your servant was in the Central Secretariat,
Wénzōng was not like that.
Déyù meant that when he was prime minister during the Tàihé period,
Wénzōng was not like this.
This trend then developed.
A ruler should simply show sincerity and trust people;
if anyone dares to deceive or mislead,
intimidate them with clear punishments.
Who would dare after that!”
The emperor approved of this.
30Wáng Yuánkuí’s vanguard had entered Xíngzhōu territory for over a month.
The Jiǔyù Zhì states: from Zhàozhōu south to Xíngzhōu territory is seventy-four lǐ.
Yuánkuí repeatedly sent secret memorials,
claiming that Hóngjìng harbored wavering intentions.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Lǐ Déyù memorialized:
“The Zhōngwǔ army has achieved success in multiple battles,
and its military prestige has risen considerably.
Wáng Zǎi is still young and strong,
and his strategies are commendable.
Since Qū Huán and Lǐ Guāngyán,
the Zhōngwǔ army has repeatedly achieved military successes.
Wáng Zǎi,
son of Zhìxīng, was probably the most outstanding among the young commanders of his time.
Given that 'Héyáng and Hédōng are both obstructed by mountains and difficult terrain,
making it impossible to advance troops;
Héyáng is obstructed by the dangers of Tàiháng,
and Hédōng by the dangers of Shíhuì and Ángchē.
閡 (hé),
read as niú dài.
Now, send Wáng Zǎi to lead the entire Zhōngwǔ army directly to Wèibó,
straight to Cízhōu,
to divide the rebel forces.'
Hóngjìng will surely be afraid.
This is a strategy to attack the mind and subvert plans.”
This was adopted.
An imperial edict ordered Zǎi to select all elite infantry and cavalry
to proceed from Xiāng and Wèi to Cízhōu.
On the Jiǎxū day,
Xuē Màoqīng broke Kēdòu Zhài,
captured Húyáng general Mǎ Jì and others,
burned and plundered seventeen small stockades,
and was only a little over ten lǐ from Huáizhōu.
Màoqīng, lacking orders from Liú Zhěn,
therefore dared not enter.
He meant he dared not enter Huáizhōu.
He believed that Liú Wù had rendered meritorious service,
and his lineage should not be severed.
Moreover,
Cóngjiàn maintained an elite army of 100,000,
with provisions for ten years.
How could it be taken!
The emperor also doubted this,
and asked Lǐ Déyù,
who replied:
“Small advances and retreats
are common in military strategy.
I wish Your Majesty would not listen to outside opinions,
then success is assured!”
The emperor then said to the prime ministers:
“Tell the court officials for me:
anyone who submits a memorial to obstruct the discussion,
I will definitely execute him on the rebel border!”
The deliberators then ceased.
Hé Hóngjìng, hearing that Wáng Zǎi was about to arrive,
feared that the Zhōngwǔ army would enter Wèi territory,
and there would be a change within his army,
so he hastily dispatched his forces.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
Hóngjìng reported that he had personally led his entire army across the Zhāngshuǐ,
heading towards Cízhōu.
On the Gēngchén day,
Lǐ Déyù memorialized:
“The Húyáng army is weak in strength,
and since the defeat at Kēdòudiàn,
the rebel forces have grown even stronger.
Wáng Màoyuán is also ill,
and morale is low,
wishing to retreat and defend Huáizhōu.
Your servant has observed that since the Yuánhé era, all rebels
have consistently targeted the weakest points of the government army,
concentrating their forces to attack them.
Once one army collapses,
they then attack other places.
Now, Wèibó has not yet fought the rebels,
and the Western Army is obstructed by difficult terrain and not advancing.
The Western Army,
refers to the Hédōng Jìn and Jiàng forces.
From Tàiháng south towards Huáizhōu is called 'below'.
Not only will this dampen military morale,
but it may also alarm Luòshī.
The Eastern Capital,
is called Luòshī.
The Luògào states: 'They arrived at Luòshī in the morning.'
Since Wèibó has already dispatched troops to attack Cízhōu,
I request an imperial edict for Wáng Zǎi to move his army.
之 (zhī),
means to go.
Not only will this protect the Eastern Capital,
but it can also exert control over Wèibó.
If the
entire army's provisions are difficult to supply,
then at least send five thousand vanguard troops to Húyáng,
which will be sufficient to boost morale.”
On the Jiǎshēn day,
he again memorialized, requesting an imperial edict for Wáng Zǎi to advance with his entire army,
and also to urgently provide equipment, silk, and cloth to aid Húyáng's distress.
The emperor approved all of his requests.
Wáng Mào-yuán 王茂元’s army was stationed at Wàn-shàn 萬善.
Liú Zhěn 劉稹 sent his牙将 (yájiàng, household general) Zhāng Jù 張巨 and Liú Gōng-zhí 劉公直, among others, to rendezvous with Xuē Mào-qīng 薛茂卿 to attack him.
They set a date to besiege Wàn-shàn 萬善 on the first day of the ninth month.
On the day yǐyǒu 乙酉,
Gōng-zhí 公直 and others secretly advanced their troops, passing five *lǐ* 里 south of Wàn-shàn 萬善.
They burned Yōng-diàn 雍店.
Jù 巨 led his army to follow,
and after passing Wàn-shàn 萬善,
he observed that the city’s defenses were weak.
Desiring to claim sole credit for the achievement,
he immediately attacked it.
As the sun began to set,
and the city was about to fall,
he sent someone to inform Gōng-zhí 公直 and the others.
At that time, the Yì-chéng 義成 army had just arrived.
As the Hé-yáng 河陽 forces were few,
Wáng Zǎi 王宰 was ordered to combine the Zhōng-wǔ 忠武 army with the Yì-chéng 義成 forces to provide reinforcement.
The Yì-chéng 義成 army
was the army from Huá-zhōu 滑州.
Wáng Mào-yuán 王茂元 wanted to lead his troops and abandon the city.
The Dū-yú-hòu 都虞候 Mèng Zhāng 孟章 admonished him,
saying:
“The enemy troops are naturally divided, some advanced, some held back;
half are at Yōng-diàn 雍店,
and half are here.
They are merely a disorganized rabble.
Now, the Yì-chéng 義成 army has just arrived
and has not yet eaten.
If they hear that the Pú-shè 僕射 (president of the Department of State Affairs) has fled,
they will collapse on their own.
Please force yourself to stay for a while!”
Mào-yuán 茂元 then stopped.
As night fell,
Gōng-zhí 公直 and the others did not arrive.
Jù 巨 withdrew his troops,
and began to ascend the mountain.
This was ascending the Tái-háng-bǎn 太行阪.
They started to alarm each other, saying:
“The pursuing troops are close!”
All fled,
and men and horses trampled each other,
with many falling into ravines and valleys to their deaths.
The emperor considered it inappropriate for Wáng Mào-yuán 王茂元 and Wáng Zǎi 王宰, two Jíedù-shǐ 節度使 (military commissioners), to both be in Hé-yáng 河陽.
On the day gēngyín 庚寅,
Lǐ Dé-yù 李德裕 and others memorialized:
“Mào-yuán 茂元 is skilled in civil administration but lacks military talent.
We request that Zǎi 宰 be appointed as the commander of the Hé-yáng 河陽 campaign army.
Once Mào-yuán 茂元 recovers from his illness,
he should merely be ordered to guard Hé-yáng 河陽.
Even if his illness worsens, it will avoid other concerns.”
In the ninth month,
on the day xīnmǎo 辛卯,
Zǎi 宰 was concurrently appointed as the commander of the Hé-yáng 河陽 campaign army.
Hé Hóng-jìng 何弘敬 memorialized that he had captured Féi-xiāng 肥鄉 and Píng-ēn 平恩.
Féi-xiāng 肥鄉
was the land of Hán-gōu 邯溝 county in the Hàn 漢 dynasty.
Cáo Wèi 曹魏 established Féi-xiāng 肥鄉 county.
By the Táng 唐 dynasty,
it, along with Píng-ēn 平恩, belonged to Míng-zhōu 洺州.
The *Jiǔ-yù Zhì* 九域志 (Record of the Nine Domains) states: Féi-xiāng 肥鄉 is thirty-five *lǐ* 里 east of the prefecture,
and Píng-ēn 平恩 is ninety *lǐ* 里 east of the prefecture.
They obtained Liú Zhěn’s 劉稹’s posters,
which all referred to the imperial army as “bandits”
and stated that they should be mercilessly slaughtered upon encounter.
On the day guǐsì 癸巳,
the emperor said to the Prime Ministers:
“Hé Hóng-jìng 何弘敬 has already captured two counties,
which can resolve previous doubts.”
This refers to Wáng Yuán-kuí 王元逵’s secret memorial that Hóng-jìng 弘敬 was playing both sides.
“Although he might wish to play both sides,
he cannot succeed.”
Thereupon, Hóng-jìng 弘ìng was promoted to concurrently hold the title of Jiǎn-xiào Zuǒ Pú-shè 檢校左僕射 (acting president of the Left Department of State Affairs).
On the day bǐngwǔ 丙午,
Hé-yáng 河陽 memorialized that Wáng Mào-yuán 王茂元 had died.
Lǐ Dé-yù 李德裕 memorialized:
“Wáng Zǎi 王宰 should only be allowed to lead the Wàn-shàn 萬善 camp troops as the Zhōng-wǔ Jíedù-shǐ 忠武節度使.
He should not be allowed to concurrently govern Hé-yáng 河陽,
lest he disregards the counties of Hé-yáng 河陽
and indulges in harassment and disturbance.
Furthermore,
the Hé-yáng Jíedù-shǐ 河陽節度使 previously held the title of Huái-zhōu Cì-shǐ 懷州刺史 (Prefect of Huái-zhōu).
A Judgement Officer often acted on his behalf.
The rent and taxes from five counties in Hé-nán 河南 were allocated to Hé-yáng 河陽.”
See volume 227 of Dè-zōng Dézōng 德宗, Jiàn-zhōng 建中 second year.
Mèng-zhōu 孟州 was established.
Mèng-zhōu 孟州 was first established
and named after Mèng-jīn 孟津.
“Once Zhāo-yì 昭義 is pacified,
Zé-zhōu 澤州 should still be allocated to the Hé-yáng Jíedù-shǐ 河陽節度使.
Then the strategic passes of Tái-háng 太行 will no longer be under Zhāo-yì 昭義,
and Hé-yáng 河陽 will become a crucial strategic point,
and the Eastern Capital will have no more worries!”
The emperor adopted his suggestion.
On the day wùshēn 戊申,
Jìng Xīn 敬昕, the Yín 尹 (Prefect) of Hé-nán 河南, was appointed as the Hé-yáng Jíedù-shǐ 河陽節度使 and Huái-mèng Guānchá-shǐ 懷孟觀察使.
Wáng Zǎi 王宰 was to lead the campaign army to resist the enemy,
while Xīn 昕 was merely to supply provisions and rations.
On the day gēngxū 庚戌,
Shí Xióng 石雄 was appointed to replace Lǐ Yàn-zuǒ 李彥佐 as the Jìn-jiàng Xíng-yíng Jíedù-shǐ 晉絳行營節度使.
*Kǎo-yì* 考異 (Textual Differences) states: The *Shí-lù* 實錄 (Veritable Records) says:
“Yàn-zuǒ 彥佐 was summoned to serve at court,
and was to proceed to his post once the military campaign ceased.”
However, Yàn-zuǒ 彥佐 had previously been dismissed from Wǔ-níng 武寧.
Now he was dismissed from Jìn-jiàng 晉絳 again.
What post was he to proceed to?
The *Shí-lù* 實錄 is mistaken.
Troops were also divided to garrison Yì-chéng 翼城 to guard against surprise attacks.

Previously,

34 The Dǎngxiàng attacked Yánzhōu.
Lǐ Yànzuǒ, formerly the Military Commissioner of Wǔníng, was appointed Military Commissioner of Shuòfāng, Líng, and Yán.

"The Dǎngxiàng are becoming increasingly rampant.

I hear that the Dǎngxiàng are scattered among various garrisons;

who are led by these various garrisons.
Each military commissioner profits from their camels and horses,
and does not capture and send them away,

Your Majesty believed that one garrison solely leading the Dǎngxiàng would grant too much power.
Your servant now requests that an imperial prince concurrently oversee these various circuits,
and select a capable and upright official from the central court to be his deputy,

Qí
was an imperial prince.
Xià
is pronounced Hùyǎfān.

The six garrisons were
Yánzhōu, Xiàzhōu, Língwǔ, Jīngyuán, as well as Zhènwǔ and Bīnníng.
35 Wǔ Hún, the Military Governor of Ānnán, compelled his officers and soldiers to build a city wall.

36 The Zhōngwǔ Army had always been renowned for its elite bravery,

Xuē Màoqīng, based on his merit at Kēdòu Zhài,

Someone said to Liú Zhěn:

He secretly colluded with Wáng Zǎi.
In the twelfth month,

Màoqīng fought a small battle,

Zǎi then burned Dà Xiǎo Jī Cūn.

Zǎi was suspicious

lured Màoqīng to Lùzhōu,

Diāohuánglǐng is located west of Chángzǐ County in Lùzhōu.

Wǔxiāng
was Hàn Yuán County,

Empress Wǔ added
the character "Wǔ"
and
it belonged to Lùzhōu.
He was Yì's nephew.
On the *wùchén* day,
Wáng Zǎi advanced to attack Zézhōu.
The *Kǎoyì* states: "A report from the *Yīpǐn Jí* dated the twenty-third day of the tenth month says:

Língchuān

Lǐ Tián, the Prefect of Míngzhōu,

Lǐ Déyù memorialized:
"Now the government armies are converging from all sides,

I request an imperial edict instructing Shí to reply to Tián's letter, saying: 'This previous letter I dare not report to the throne.

The *Kǎoyì* states: A report from the *Yīpǐn Jí* dated the fourth day of the first month states:

Déyù's memorial was submitted on the fourth day of the first month,

The Emperor was enraged
